summary.intent: Land a stacked PR (on top of #242) fixing staging and `add` race conditions in the callisto repo, addressing Codex review findings plus a failure when the lockfile or changelog is git-ignored.
summary.outcome: Linked #241 and #242 as a native GitHub stack (#243), implemented the staging, exclusive-create and ignored-file probe fixes with unit and e2e tests, updated specs, docs and a changeset, ran CI green (92.73% coverage), then committed, pushed and opened the stacked PR.

repo: Work is done in git worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ (e.g. stage-and-race), and CI is run as a full pipeline command that can be backgrounded and reports completion via task notification.
Changes to user-facing behavior require a changeset in .changeset/, updates to docs/errors.md, and matching criteria in docs/specs/cli.json and docs/specs/versioning.json.
Many apply tests in callisto-graph use fake CommandRunners that return exit 0 for every command, so any new git invocation must be designed so a blanket 'exit 0' does not read as a meaningful result.
Ignored-file detection uses `git check-ignore`; the final approach is non-quiet mode, treating only printed output as 'ignored', rather than relying on exit status alone or parsing output.
The `add` command's filename selection was racy; the fix uses exclusive-create in callisto-model's atomic.rs so concurrent adds do not overwrite each other.

code.finding: Atomic write helpers were extended with exclusive-create semantics to close the `add` filename-selection race.
Preflight now probes whether targets are stageable (not git-ignored) before applying, using non-quiet `git check-ignore` where printed output indicates ignored.
New e2e tests cover the ignored-lockfile and ignored-changelog scenarios.

workflow: Use `gh stack link` to join dependent PRs into a native GitHub stack and base each new PR on the previous one.
Python scratchpad scripts were used for multi-file edits; commit messages and PR bodies were written to scratchpad files and passed to git/gh.
Run lint then the full CI pipeline locally before pushing, and run it in the background while waiting.

friction: The first quiet `git check-ignore` approach broke several apply tests because fake runners return exit 0 for everything, requiring a redesign to the non-quiet, output-based check.
Needed to check whether CommandRunner supports stdin before choosing the check-ignore invocation, which cost an extra iteration.
The first test run produced failures that needed a separate step to read the failure messages.
open_items: The new PR still needs to be added to the native GitHub stack after opening (stacked on #242).
The preflight guarantee was scoped in the spec because it cannot cover every race, so remaining TOCTOU windows between preflight and apply may deserve follow-up.
